headline: Rakuten Securities' second report confirms a leak of about 4.41 million people's details; the cause is still not given.
summary: Added the company's Nov 24 second report (s023 notice, s024 press release, both Tier 1, Japanese, translated by us) and the Mainichi Shimbun report of it (s025, Tier 2). c002 now records that the company says the data was taken outside (no longer only a possible leak). c003: about 4.41 million people (3.22 million account holders, 1.19 million who never opened an account; may include duplicates), seven more data items, assets by product for about 1.68 million, self-reported assets about 2.71 million and income about 14,000 (brackets only). c004: login IDs only for about 11.98 million accounts (was up to 11.25 million); no combined total given, so the 15.72M figure is retired. c005 restated on Nov 24. c009, c010, c011 still Not established: no cause, attacker or ransom claim. headline: Rakuten Securities says it will report its investigation results, but has not said how or when.
summary: Added 2 Tier 2 sources from J-CAST News. J-CAST (Nov 20, s021) reports the company said it will report its investigation results by some method when it can, and that the format, including whether to hold a press conference, is still being considered; added to c009, which stays Not established. J-CAST (Nov 18, s022, via Yahoo! News) reports the company said it confirmed the leak actually happened, that the two account groups do not overlap, and that production data was moved to the test environment temporarily for upgrade checks; added to c002, c004 and c013, labels unchanged. The company declined to comment on compensation. No company notice after Nov 19 (direct notice URLs for Nov 21-23 return 404), no FSA page, cause, attacker, ransom claim, compensation, count change or answer on masking; c007 stays Reported. headline: Rakuten Securities later confirmed the test-environment data actually leaked, Nikkei xTECH reports.
summary: Added 2 Tier 2 sources found this run, both from Nov 17-18: Nikkei xTECH (s019) and INTERNET Watch (s020). Nikkei xTECH reports the company said that, after its Nov 17 notice, it confirmed the leak actually happened, and that the two account groups do not overlap. These are added to c002 and c004; both labels stay Confirmed as the company's account. INTERNET Watch reports the company said the two groups cover nearly all of its accounts, and both outlets relay the company's explanation that production data was used to check a system upgrade (c013). There is still no company notice after Nov 19, no FSA page, cause, attacker, ransom claim, compensation, count change or answer on masking; c007 stays Reported. headline: Rakuten Securities says its systems were breached; how, and by whom, is not established.
summary: First draft. 7 sources (2 Tier 1, 4 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 12 claims (7 Confirmed, 1 Reported, 4 Not established), 9 questions. Rakuten Securities says a third party gained unauthorized access, that test-environment data on up to about 15.72 million accounts may have leaked on Nov 11, and that it has not confirmed any password or PIN leak or any related fraudulent trade; the label Confirmed records that these are the company's statements. Japan's Financial Services Agency ordered a report on Nov 19. The unmasked-data-in-test-environment account is Reported from one Tier 3 outlet. Cause, attacker, ransom claims and links to other Rakuten incidents are Not established. We did not visit any leak site, dark-web page or tracker. The company notices are in Japanese and were translated by us. Privacy check done: no names of officials, reporters or spokespeople, no handles, contact details or phone numbers.
